slot.brief: A bridge with four resistors; identify the condition for balance and find the unknown resistance for zero galvanometer deflection.

stem: In the bridge shown, the galvanometer gives zero deflection. What is the value of the unknown resistance $R$?

verdicts.working: At balance, the potential drops from A to C and A to D are equal: 9/(9+15) = 12/(12+R). Solving gives R = 20 Ω.

working:
At balance: $\dfrac{R_{AC}}{R_{CB}}=\dfrac{R_{AD}}{R_{DB}}$.
$\dfrac{9}{15}=\dfrac{12}{R}$
$R=\dfrac{15\times12}{9}=20\ \Omega$

Independent check: At balance, the potential drops from A to C and A to D are equal: 9/(9+15) = 12/(12+R). Solving gives R = 20 Ω.
solution:
At balance, the bridge ratio is $\dfrac{R_{AC}}{R_{CB}}=\dfrac{R_{AD}}{R_{DB}}$.
$$\dfrac{9}{15}=\dfrac{12}{R}\quad\Rightarrow\quad R=\dfrac{15\times12}{9}=20\ \Omega$$

draft.stem: In the bridge shown, the galvanometer gives zero deflection. What is the value of the unknown resistance $R$?

figure.description: Draw a Wheatstone bridge as a diamond with top node A, bottom node B, left midpoint C and right midpoint D. Connect a cell between A and B. Connect a 9 Ω resistor between A and C, a 15 Ω resistor between C and B, a 12 Ω resistor between A and D, and an unknown resistor labelled R between D and B. Connect a galvanometer between C and D. Label all four nodes and all components; show no current direction arrows.

draft.distractor_notes: A: Uses $R=9\times12/15$, interchanging the ratio. B: Uses $R=9\times15/12$, pairing the wrong arms. D: Incorrectly adds the two resistors on one side instead of applying the balance condition.
